title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ecclesiastes chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ecclesiastes Chapter 7.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 7:1, what is better than precious ointment?
questions.correctAnswer: A good name
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:1 states that a good name is better than precious ointment.

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 7:2, which is said to be better to go to?
questions.correctAnswer: House of mourning
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:2 says it is better to go to the house of mourning than to the house of feasting.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 7:3 say is better than laughter?
questions.correctAnswer: Sorrow
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:3 states that sorrow is better than laughter.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 7:4 says that the heart of fools is in the house of mourning.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:4 says the heart of fools is in the house of mirth, not mourning.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 7:5, what is better to hear than the song of fools?
questions.correctAnswer: The rebuke of the wise
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:5 says it is better to hear the rebuke of the wise than the song of fools.

questions.question: Ecclesiastes 7:6 compares the laughter of the fool to what?
options: Crackling of thorns under a pot
questions.correctAnswer: Crackling of thorns under a pot
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:6 compares the laughter of the fool to the crackling of thorns under a pot.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 7:7 says that oppression makes a wise man mad.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:7 states that oppression maketh a wise man mad.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 7:8, what is better than the beginning of a thing?
questions.correctAnswer: The end of a thing
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:8 says better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof.

questions.question: Ecclesiastes 7:9 advises not to be hasty in what emotion?
questions.correctAnswer: Anger
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:9 warns not to be hasty in thy spirit to be angry.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 7:10 tells us to wisely inquire about why former days were better than these.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:10 says not to enquire wisely about why former days were better, implying it is unwise to do so.

questions.question: Which is better according to Ecclesiastes 7:8?
questions.correctAnswer: The patient in spirit
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:8 says the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 7, which instruction comes first?
options: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise
A good name is better than precious ointment
Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry
Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof
questions.correctAnswer: A good name is better than precious ointment
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:1 is the first instruction given among these options.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 7:3 indicates that sadness improves the heart.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:3 says by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.

questions.question: Ecclesiastes 7:2 says the living will lay to their heart what event?
questions.correctAnswer: The end of all men
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:2 explains that the living will lay to heart the end of all men.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 7:5, hearing the rebuke of the wise is better than hearing what?
questions.correctAnswer: The song of fools
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:5 compares hearing the rebuke of the wise to hearing the song of fools, stating the former is better.

medium.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ecclesiastes Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 7:11, what benefit does wisdom bring along with an inheritance?
options: It brings profit to those who live
questions.correctAnswer: It brings profit to those who live
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:11 states that wisdom is good along with an inheritance and that it brings profit to those who see the sun, meaning those who live and experience life.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 7:12 say is the excellency of knowledge compared to wisdom and money?
options: It gives life to those who have it
questions.correctAnswer: It gives life to those who have it
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:12 explains that while wisdom and money are defenses, the excellency of knowledge is that wisdom gives life to those who possess it.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 7:13 encourage believers to consider about God's work?
options: Who can straighten what God has made crooked
questions.correctAnswer: Who can straighten what God has made crooked
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:13 urges us to consider that no one can make straight what God has made crooked, emphasizing acceptance of God's sovereign work.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 7:14 teach us to respond to prosperity and adversity?
options: Be joyful in prosperity and consider adversity thoughtfully
questions.correctAnswer: Be joyful in prosperity and consider adversity thoughtfully
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:14 instructs believers to rejoice in prosperous days but to thoughtfully consider adversity, acknowledging that both are set by God for a purpose.

questions.question: What paradox about the fate of the righteous and the wicked is described in Ecclesiastes 7:15?
options: A just man may perish in his righteousness, and a wicked man may prolong life in wickedness
Only the righteous live long lives
questions.correctAnswer: A just man may perish in his righteousness, and a wicked man may prolong life in wickedness
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:15 reveals the paradox that sometimes the just perish despite their righteousness, while the wicked may live long despite their wickedness.

questions.question: What practical wisdom does Ecclesiastes 7:16 give regarding righteousness and wisdom?
options: Be excessively righteous and overly wise
Avoid being overly righteous or overly wise to prevent self-destruction
Seek only righteousness and reject wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Avoid being overly righteous or overly wise to prevent self-destruction
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:16 advises against being excessively righteous or overly wise because doing so may lead to self-destruction, promoting balance in Christian living.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 7:17 warn against extremes in behavior?
options: Be excessively wicked to avoid early death
Avoid both excessive wickedness and foolishness to prevent dying before your time
questions.correctAnswer: Avoid both excessive wickedness and foolishness to prevent dying before your time
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:17 cautions not to be overly wicked or foolish, as these extremes can cause premature death, promoting moderation and wisdom.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 7:18, what is the outcome for one who fears God?
options: They will come forth better than all
They will be destroyed by folly
questions.correctAnswer: They will come forth better than all
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:18 states that the one who fears God will come forth better than all, highlighting the value of reverence for God in overcoming life's challenges.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 7:19 say about the strength wisdom provides compared to physical might?
options: Wisdom is weaker than ten mighty men
Wisdom strengthens the wise more than ten mighty men in the city
Physical strength is more valuable than wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom strengthens the wise more than ten mighty men in the city
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:19 highlights that wisdom provides greater strength and advantage than even ten mighty men, emphasizing the power of wisdom over physical strength.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 7:20 reveal about human righteousness?
options: There is a perfectly just man on earth
No one on earth does good without sinning
questions.correctAnswer: No one on earth does good without sinning
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:20 acknowledges that no man on earth is perfectly just or sinless, reminding believers of human imperfection and the need for God's grace.

questions.question: What connection can be drawn between Ecclesiastes 7:16 and 7:17 regarding living wisely?
options: Both warn against excess in righteousness, wisdom, wickedness, and foolishness to avoid self-destruction or premature death
questions.correctAnswer: Both warn against excess in righteousness, wisdom, wickedness, and foolishness to avoid self-destruction or premature death
questions.explanation: Verses 7:16 and 7:17 together counsel moderation, warning that excess in righteousness or wisdom as well as wickedness or foolishness leads to harm or early death, encouraging balanced living.

questions.question: If one follows the advice in Ecclesiastes 7:14 to be joyful in prosperity and consider adversity, what insight from Ecclesiastes 7:13 supports this attitude?
options: That God has made crooked things which no one can straighten
That we should avoid all difficulties
questions.correctAnswer: That God has made crooked things which no one can straighten
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:13 helps us understand that God's sovereign work includes crookedness that cannot be changed, supporting the attitude in 7:14 to accept both joy and adversity as God's design.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 7:18 teach about the relationship between fearing God and human behavior discussed in verses 16 and 17?
options: Fearing God leads to balanced living, avoiding extremes in righteousness, wisdom, wickedness, and foolishness
Fearing God encourages excess in righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: Fearing God leads to balanced living, avoiding extremes in righteousness, wisdom, wickedness, and foolishness
questions.explanation: Verse 7:18 highlights that fearing God results in better conduct, correlating with verses 7:16-17 which warn against excess and encourage moderation in living.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 7:12 states that money alone is the best defense for life.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:12 states that both wisdom and money are defenses, but the excellency of knowledge is that wisdom gives life. It does not say money alone is the best defense.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 7:20 teaches that there is no perfectly just person on earth who never sins.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:20 clearly states that there is no just man upon earth who does good and sins not, emphasizing the imperfection of humans.

hard.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ecclesiastes Chapter 7.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 7, what is recommended instead of heeding all spoken words to avoid hearing curses?
options: Ignore some words to avoid hearing curses
questions.correctAnswer: Ignore some words to avoid hearing curses
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:21 advises to take no heed unto all words spoken to avoid hearing curses from your servant.

questions.question: What does the preacher acknowledge about his own wisdom in Ecclesiastes 7?
options: He became the wisest man on earth
He intended to be wise but found it far from him
questions.correctAnswer: He intended to be wise but found it far from him
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:23 states that though he said, 'I will be wise,' wisdom was far from him.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 7:24 describe as 'far off, and exceeding deep' and difficult to find out?
options: That which is far off and exceeding deep
questions.correctAnswer: That which is far off and exceeding deep
questions.explanation: Verse 24 speaks about things that are far off and deep, specifically stating that no one can find them out.

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 7:25, what three things does the preacher apply his heart to search and seek?
options: Wisdom, the reason of things, and the wickedness of folly
The law, the prophets, and the psalms
The creation, the flood, and the exile
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom, the reason of things, and the wickedness of folly
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says he sought wisdom, the reason of things, and the wickedness of folly, foolishness, and madness.

questions.question: Ecclesiastes 7:26 uses a metaphor describing a woman whose heart is snares and nets. What is said about those who please God and sinners in relation to her?
options: Whoso pleaseth God shall escape her, but the sinner shall be taken
All men shall be caught by her
She is a symbol of salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Whoso pleaseth God shall escape her, but the sinner shall be taken
questions.explanation: Verse 26 clearly states that those who please God escape from the woman (a metaphor for temptation or evil), but sinners are caught by her.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 7:28, how many men and women did the preacher find among thousands?
options: One man among a thousand; no woman among all
One woman among a thousand; no man among all
questions.correctAnswer: One man among a thousand; no woman among all
questions.explanation: The verse states he found one man among a thousand but no woman among all those.

questions.question: What fundamental truth about mankind does Ecclesiastes 7:29 reveal according to the preacher?
options: God made man upright, but they sought out many inventions
Man is inherently sinful and corrupt
Man was created to be perfect
God made man sinful from birth
questions.correctAnswer: God made man upright, but they sought out many inventions
questions.explanation: Verse 29 says God made man upright, but mankind has sought out many inventions, indicating corruption through human creativity or deviation.

questions.question: Which other scripture passage echoes the theme of human imperfection and sinfulness found in Ecclesiastes 7:20?
options: Romans 3:10 - There is none righteous, no, not one
Psalm 23:1 - The Lord is my shepherd
Genesis 1:1 - In the beginning God created
John 3:16 - For God so loved the world
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 3:10 - There is none righteous, no, not one
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:20 states there is not a just man who does good and sins not, which echoes Romans 3:10 about universal human sinfulness.

questions.question: What literary device is most apparent in the structure of Ecclesiastes 7:8 comparing the end of a thing to its beginning and contrasting patient and proud spirits?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Verse 8 uses parallelism by contrasting 'the end of a thing' with 'the beginning' and 'patient in spirit' with 'proud in spirit'.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 7:12, what is the excellence of knowledge compared to wisdom and money?
options: Wisdom gives life to those who have it
Money is more valuable than wisdom
Wisdom and money are equally excellent
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom gives life to those who have it
questions.explanation: Verse 12 states that while wisdom and money are defenses, the excellence of knowledge is that wisdom gives life to those who have it.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 7:9 advise about the emotion of anger?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse advises not to be hasty to anger because anger rests in the bosom of fools, making 'True' the correct answer.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 7:16, is being overly righteous encouraged for a long and meaningful life?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 16 warns against being overly righteous or wise because it could lead to self-destruction, so 'False' is correct.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'snare' in Ecclesiastes 7:26 imply about the nature of the woman described?
options: A trap or entanglement leading to ruin
A source of joy and blessing
questions.correctAnswer: A trap or entanglement leading to ruin
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'mokan' (מָכוֹן) translated as 'snare' implies a trap or entanglement, signifying danger and ruin as in verse 26.

questions.question: Ecclesiastes 7:14 presents a principle about prosperity and adversity. What is the reason given for God setting these opposites?
options: So that man should find nothing after him
questions.correctAnswer: So that man should find nothing after him
questions.explanation: Verse 14 explains that God sets prosperity and adversity over against each other so that man should ultimately find nothing after him.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book contains a similar reflection on the fleeting nature of human life and the pursuit of wisdom as seen in Ecclesiastes 7?
questions.correctAnswer: Job
questions.explanation: The book of Job, like Ecclesiastes 7, deeply reflects on human suffering, the search for wisdom, and the brevity of life.

theological.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ecclesiastes Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What is said to be better than precious ointment?
questions.correctAnswer: A good name
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:1 states, 'A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one's birth.' This emphasizes the value of reputation over material wealth.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 7, what is better than laughter?
questions.correctAnswer: Sorrow
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:3 states, 'Sorrow is better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.' This suggests that sorrow can lead to personal growth.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 7:4 suggest about the hearts of the wise and fools?
options: The wise are in mourning, fools in mirth
questions.correctAnswer: The wise are in mourning, fools in mirth
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:4 indicates, 'The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth,' signifying the different priorities of wise and foolish people.

questions.question: What is said to be better than the song of fools?
questions.correctAnswer: The advice of the wise
questions.explanation: According to Ecclesiastes 7:5, 'It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools,' highlighting the value of wise counsel over foolish entertainment.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 7:7 say about oppression and gifts?
options: They can lead to madness and heart destruction
questions.correctAnswer: They can lead to madness and heart destruction
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:7 states, 'Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad; and a gift destroyeth the heart,' indicating the negative impact of oppression and the corrupting nature of gifts.

questions.question: What is better according to Ecclesiastes 7:8?
questions.correctAnswer: The end of a thing
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:8 asserts, 'Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof,' suggesting that the outcomes of actions are more significant than their initial stages.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 7:10, what is advised against?
questions.correctAnswer: Longing for the past
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:10 advises, 'Say not thou, What is the cause that the former days were better than these?' suggesting that such thoughts are unwise.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 7:12 say is better than money?
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:12 states, 'For wisdom is a defence, and money is a defence: but the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom giveth life to them that have it,' highlighting the superior value of wisdom.

questions.question: What insight does Ecclesiastes 7:15 provide about the just and wicked?
options: The righteous may suffer while the wicked thrive
All men are equal in death
questions.correctAnswer: The righteous may suffer while the wicked thrive
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:15 indicates, 'there is a just man that perisheth in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man that prolongeth his life in his wickedness,' demonstrating the complexities of justice.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 7:19 say about wisdom?
options: It is only for the rich
questions.correctAnswer: It is better than strength
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:19 states, 'Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty men which are in the city,' emphasizing the superior strength that wisdom provides.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 7:20, what is the condition of humanity?
questions.correctAnswer: All sin
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:20 asserts, 'For there is not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not,' indicating the universal condition of sinfulness among humanity.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 7:26 suggest about women?
options: They can be a source of bitterness
They are not to be trusted
questions.correctAnswer: They can be a source of bitterness
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:26 states, 'And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets,' indicating a cautionary perspective on certain relationships.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Ecclesiastes 7:8 and 7:9 convey about patience and pride?
questions.correctAnswer: Patience is better than pride
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:8 emphasizes the value of patience, while 7:9 warns against hasty anger, together indicating that patience is preferable to pride and impulsiveness.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that wisdom is irrelevant in a world filled with injustice. What does Ecclesiastes 7:15-20 actually teach?
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom provides strength and understanding
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:15-20 reveals that while injustice exists, wisdom still strengthens the wise and helps them navigate life's complexities, thus affirming its relevance.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 7:29 reveal about the nature of humanity?
options: Humanity is made upright but seeks evil
questions.correctAnswer: Humanity is made upright but seeks evil
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 7:29 states, 'Lo, this only have I found, that God hath made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions,' indicating that humans were created good but have turned to their own ways.
